message.content: {"predictors": [{"name": "Customer Concentration Ratio", "construction": "Sum the revenue attributed to the firm's top 3 customers (from 10-K disclosures), divided by total revenues, measured annually.", "rationale": "Firms with lower customer concentration are less exposed to idiosyncratic shocks and have more diversified revenue streams, potentially making them less risky and more likely to be undervalued.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Short-Term Asset Reinvestment Rate", "construction": "Annual change in short-term investments (balance sheet) divided by total assets at the start of the year.", "rationale": "Firms aggressively reinvesting in liquid assets may signal underutilization of capital or lack of investment opportunities.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Patent Intensity", "construction": "Number of new patents granted to a firm in the past 12 months (USPTO data) divided by total assets.", "rationale": "Innovative firms may be undervalued if the market underappreciates the value of intellectual property.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Cash Conversion Cycle Change", "construction": "Change in cash conversion cycle (days inventory outstanding + days sales outstanding - days payables outstanding) over the last year.", "rationale": "Firms that improve their cash conversion cycles may be improving operational efficiency, which the market may not immediately price.", "higher_returns_for": "large negative changes (i.e., improvements)"}, {"name": "Dividend Cut Frequency", "construction": "Number of dividend cuts in the past 5 years divided by number of years with positive dividends.", "rationale": "Frequent dividend cuts may indicate management instability or poor capital allocation, leading to persistent undervaluation.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "R&D-to-Depreciation Ratio", "construction": "R&D expense (income statement) divided by depreciation expense, measured annually.", "rationale": "A higher ratio suggests forward-looking investment relative to replacement of old assets, potentially linked to future growth underestimated by the market.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Management Tenure Consistency", "construction": "Standard deviation of CEO tenure (in years) among S&P 1500 firms in the same GICS industry; assign this industry-level measure to each firm.", "rationale": "Industries with less management churn may enable long-term strategy and better firm performance not yet reflected in prices.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Legal Expense Ratio", "construction": "Total legal expenses (from footnotes in 10-K) divided by sales, measured annually.", "rationale": "High legal expenses may indicate persistent underlying risks or inefficiencies not fully priced in.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Inventory Obsolescence Provision Trend", "construction": "Three-year trend (slope) in inventory obsolescence provisions (from 10-K footnotes) as a percent of total inventory.", "rationale": "Decreasing provisions may signal improving inventory quality and better sales prospects overlooked by the market.", "higher_returns_for": "strong negative slopes (declining provisions)"}, {"name": "Board Director Age Dispersion", "construction": "Standard deviation of ages of board directors, measured annually from proxy statements.", "rationale": "Greater age diversity may indicate a broader range of perspectives and better governance, potentially resulting in superior performance.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}]}
